note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute shortness of breath for approximately 1 hour while sitting watching TV. No specific trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Cough began yesterday; shortness of breath started over the last hour and was described as sudden/recent.
  - Patient reports increasing anxiety and perception of an elevated heart rate.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: Not reported.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: Not reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: Not reported.
  - Drooling: Not reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: Not reported.
  - Dyspnea: Reported (acute onset, current).
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): Not reported.
  - Ear/neck symptoms: Not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar episodes reported.
  - Recent cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
  - No prior hospitalizations or injections for this problem documented.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergy: Ibuprofen — reaction not documented.
  - Current medication: Codeine — dose/route/frequency not documented; patient has been taking it fairly regularly for post-C-section pain but probably stopped ~1 week ago.
- Relevant social context:
  - Patient is postpartum and currently with her baby. Partner not at home (at work). Patient is alone with the infant and will travel to hospital with the baby.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: None stated.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: Shortness of breath reported; no stridor or noisy breathing documented.
- Mental status and associated features: Patient anxious/stressed, reporting palpitations ("my heart, it's really going"), able to converse and follow instructions.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded. Patient counted "30" beats during the clinician-guided pulse count; clinician interpreted this as "slightly fast." No objective heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, or exam findings documented.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Baby present with patient.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
  - Acute shortness of breath in a postpartum patient (4 weeks post–cesarean) — clinician concerned about possible venous thromboembolism/pulmonary embolism given recent surgery and sudden onset dyspnea.
  - Anxiety and palpitations noted; cough since yesterday may be concurrent but no productive sputum reported.
- Key justifications from the transcript:
  - Recent C-section (4 weeks prior) with new, sudden-onset shortness of breath.
  - Clinician explicitly stated concern for clots that can occur after C-section and present in the legs or lungs.
- Conflict noted: None identified.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Patient advised to go to hospital promptly for further evaluation (clinician recommended hospital assessment).
  - Clinician offered to call an ambulance; patient declined and chose to travel to hospital with her baby.
  - Patient advised not to take Codeine for the time being prior to hospital attendance.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver:
  - "Go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time."
  - Option explained: clinician can call an ambulance or patient can take herself; patient elected to self-transport.
- Escalation criteria / red flags (as discussed or implied):
  - Worsening shortness of breath, breathing difficulty, or other signs suggestive of cardiopulmonary compromise — proceed to emergency care (ambulance option was offered).
- Follow-up:
  - Immediate hospital assessment planned; further management (e.g., anticoagulation if clot confirmed) to be determined in hospital.
  - No ENT/allergy referral or auto-injector discussion documented.
- Emergency contact instructions exactly as stated in transcript:
  - Clinician offered to "call an ambulance" as one option for transport to hospital.

Document_quality (Quality checks)
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation).
  - Physical examination of chest/lungs, cardiovascular exam, and lower limbs for DVT signs.
  - History of prior thromboembolic events, anticoagulant use, or thrombophilia.
  - Details of the ibuprofen allergy reaction.
  - Exact dose/route/frequency of Codeine.
  - Any prior pregnancy/postpartum complications.
  - Smoking status and other VTE risk factors.
  - Availability of support for childcare and safe transport arrangements.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/transcript clear and intelligible; content adequate for above documentation.
